ORIGINAL:EO:3108.text:
Executive Other,
The Civil Service Commission n-iay enter upon its register for stenographer,
typewriter, or stenographer and typewriter at Washington, D. C., or elsewhere,
the name of a person certified and appointed within three years from any of
these registers who is found to he assigned principally in point of time or im-
portance to work not requiring proficiency in the technical subjects upon which
he was examined, after the following procedure:
(n) The employee shall transmit request for entry of his name on the register
through the head of his department or office or his authorized representative,
in which he shall state the kind or kinds of work he is performing and the amount
of time devoted to each kind.
(2) The request shall be promptly forwarded to the Commission with com-
meat or reconiwendation.
(3) If the Commission finds that the principal duties of the person are not
those requiring proficiency in the technical subjects upon which he was ex-
amined, his naive shall be entered upon the appropriate register for further
certification unless the dlepartmlent or office corrects the assignment and so
reports.
(q~.) No disciplinary measure or discrimiination shall follow request under
this order except for false statement therein, of which the Commission shall be
the judge.
(5) A person certified and selected under the terms ot this order shall be at
liberty to accept appointment without objection or hindrance by the (depart-
mnent or office which failed to assign him to duties in keeping with his examina-
tion.WOODROW WILSON
Tim W rVnITE Hou~se,
